title: Supervisory Stress Test Documentation Market Risk Models

source.name: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

summary: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System released technical model documentation for the 2026 Supervisory Stress Test covering eight market risk models. The document details the Securities, Fair Value Option, Yield Curve, Private Equity, Trading Profit and Loss, Trading Issuer Default Loss, CVA, and Largest Counterparty Default (LCPD) Models. Originally published October 2025, it was updated January 2026.
key_points: Covers eight market risk models intended for use in the 2026 DFA Supervisory Stress Test cycle
Securities Model includes Fair Value Model, Credit Loss Model, and OCI Calculation components
Yield Curve Model covers Treasury, SOFR, and Corporate segments separately
Trading Profit and Loss Model comprises Market Value Component and Sensitivity-Based Component
CVA Model includes both Standard and Non-Standard variants
LCPD Model addresses Largest Counterparty Default risk scenarios
Document was updated January 2026, superseding the October 2025 initial release
why_it_matters: Banks subject to DFA stress testing requirements need this technical documentation to understand how the Fed calculates stress losses across trading operations, securities portfolios, and counterparty exposures. Model transparency enables institutions to better prepare for annual supervisory stress tests and calibrate internal risk estimates.
market_structure_context: This documentation provides transparency into Federal Reserve supervisory stress test methodologies, revealing how the central bank assesses market risk across trading books, securities portfolios, and counterparty credit exposures under the DFA framework.
